transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the biggest reason I’m here is my sleep. It’s gotten really unreliable, to the point where even when I’m completely exhausted and I get into bed thinking I should just pass out, I don’t. I’ll just lie there with my mind going over sales forecasts, numbers, conversations with people on my team, things I should’ve handled differently, things I need to handle tomorrow… it just keeps looping.

And then if I do fall asleep, I’m waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and it’s like my brain turns back on full speed. I’ll try to tell myself, “Just go back to sleep,” but then I’m thinking through work issues again, or anticipating problems, and I can’t seem to power down. It’s been really frustrating because I feel like I’m doing all the right things by going to bed, but my mind won’t cooperate.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I definitely have nights where I sleep very little, but I don’t wake up feeling great or energized. It’s more like I’m dragging myself through the day and trying to function on fumes.

There have been times at work where I’ve had to push through and maybe I look “on” because I’m in meetings or managing people, but internally I don’t feel unusually powered up or anything. It’s more like stress and adrenaline keeping me going, if that makes sense. I wouldn’t say I’ve had a stretch where I needed less sleep and felt totally fine or better than usual.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things, not just work?

Yes… definitely. Work is the biggest thing, just because it’s always right in front of me, but it’s not only work. My mind sort of jumps around all day. I’ll be thinking about whether we’re going to hit the launch numbers, and then suddenly I’m wondering if someone on my team is unhappy and about to quit, and then somehow I’m thinking about the mortgage, or whether a client renewal is going to fall through.

It’s like one concern leads into another, and even small things don’t feel small in my head. If someone takes too long to respond to an email, or there’s a minor delay, I start imagining how it could turn into a much bigger problem. I know not all of it is logical, but in the moment it feels hard to stop following the chain of “what ifs.”
Did this start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

It wasn’t like one single dramatic thing happened, exactly, but I can trace it pretty clearly to the sales division reorganization. That was about… thirteen months ago now, I think. Around then is when things started feeling like they were shifting under my feet, and since then it’s just been building.

At first I told myself it was normal because any reorg is stressful, and everyone was kind of on edge. But it didn’t really settle down for me afterward. It’s more like that change started the pattern, and then over the months it became more constant. So yes, there was a work change that seems tied to when this all began, but it didn’t feel like an overnight switch—more like it gradually ramped up after that.
Have you been feeling this level of worry more days than not for at least six months?

Yes. I mean, if I’m being honest, it’s been much longer than six months at this point. It’s been building since the sales division reorganization, which was about thirteen months ago.

At first I kept thinking, “Okay, this is just temporary, things are unsettled, everyone’s stressed,” but it didn’t really go away. It became more of the normal background noise in my head. Some days are worse than others, obviously, but overall, yes—it’s been there more days than not for well over six months.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or you can’t relax?

Yes, very much. I feel kind of wound up almost all the time, like my body is bracing for something even when there’s nothing actually happening right then.

The best way I can describe it is… it’s like I’m sitting in a pipeline review or waiting to be put on the spot, even when I’m just at home eating dinner. My shoulders are probably the biggest thing I notice—they’re always up around my ears, and I’ll realize I’ve been holding them tight for ages. I try to consciously relax them, and for maybe thirty seconds it helps, but then they’re tight again without me even noticing.

It’s not like normal “I had a long day” tension either. It feels like my body doesn’t really get the message that I’m allowed to relax. Even if I sit on the couch or try to have a quiet evening, I still feel keyed up inside, like I’m waiting for the next thing to go wrong.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to control or stop the worry?

Yes. That’s actually one of the most frustrating parts, because it feels like I should be able to stop it once I’ve thought something through.

Like, I’ll tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve done the plan, you’ve looked at the numbers, you’ve thought through what you need to do—let it go.” And for a minute I’ll feel like, okay, fine, I’ve handled that concern. But then five minutes later I’m right back in another loop. It’s like I check one worry off the list and then three more pop up immediately.

And it’s not even always that the worry is new or useful. Sometimes it’s the same thing from a slightly different angle, or I’m replaying whether I missed something, or imagining some other outcome. I’ll try to reason with myself, but it doesn’t really stay put. My brain just keeps grabbing onto the next possible problem.
Do you often feel tired or easily fatigued during the day?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I do have days where I feel tired, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m easily fatigued in a really obvious way.

Part of me feels like… well, everybody in my job is tired, right? So I have a hard time separating what’s normal work exhaustion from something else. I can usually still get through the day and do what I need to do, but I wouldn’t say I feel especially refreshed or energetic most of the time either.

So… maybe a little, but it’s not the main thing I notice. It’s more that I feel worn down sometimes, but I haven’t really been tracking whether that’s happening every day or anything like that.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because your mind goes blank or gets pulled into worry?

I’m not completely sure. I mean, I do get distracted sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d describe it as my mind going blank exactly.

There are moments where I’ll be trying to focus on something and then realize I’ve drifted off into thinking about something else, but I’m not sure how much of that is unusual. With work especially, there are a lot of moving pieces, so it’s hard to tell whether I’m having trouble concentrating because of worry or because there’s just always something competing for attention.

I wouldn’t say I’ve really tracked it closely. I notice the worrying more than I notice the concentration part, if that makes sense. Like, I can usually still finish what I’m doing, but sometimes it takes more effort to pull myself back on task.
Has this worrying been interfering with how you function at work or at home?

Yes, it has. I wish I could say it’s just happening in my head and not really affecting anything, but it has started spilling over.

At work, especially, I notice it during pipeline reviews or when I’m making decisions about forecasts or next steps with the team. I’ll second-guess myself so much that what should be a pretty straightforward conversation gets tense. I’ll go back over the same point more than once, or I’ll ask for more reassurance than I probably need, and then I can feel the room getting kind of tight. It’s not that I can’t do my job, but it takes more energy than it should, and I think people can tell I’m wound up.

And then by the time I get home, I’m just… spent. My husband will be trying to talk to me about normal things, or even just asking a simple question, and I’m not as present as I want to be. I can be short or reactive, not because he did anything wrong, but because I’ve used up so much energy all day managing the worry and rethinking everything. So yes, it’s affecting both. Not totally ruining everything, but definitely interfering more than I’d like.
